source.instructions: Anchises Analysis is a read-only stock screening and analysis service. In public access mode no login is required; all callers share global rate and concurrency limits. Full market datasets may be used for server-side filtering and aggregate analysis, but row-level results shown to the host are limited to the first 200 rows with no next-page cursor or SQL OFFSET. Never reconstruct a dataset by splitting filters, dates, fields, or sort ranges. CSV export is available only for selective screen_stocks results: at most 1,000 rows, 25 columns, 20,000 cells, Top-N 200, or 50 explicit tickers, and never an exact complete exchange-day partition. Raw SQL results cannot be exported. If export is refused, continue with server-side analysis or suggest a narrower research question. CSV download URLs are bearer capabilities and must not be shared. Before stock-data or company-report calls, resolve a company name or ticker to exchange, ticker, and company name; use chat context and primary web sources to disambiguate when needed. Company-report requests always use prepare_company_report_generation and live host-side research; the server does not read cached reports, PDFs, or expiry state. It only selects and returns one sector prompt. Anchises Analysis does not search the web or write, cache, upload, save, or publish the resulting report; a compatible host must perform live web research and reply in the current conversation. External, inactive, delisted, and unmatched companies use the Others prompt and require identity and listing-status verification. ETF and fund instruments are not eligible. Never ask users to paste credentials or tokens into chat.

tools.name: get_connection_status
tools.title: Get Anchises Analysis connection status
tools.description: Use this when you need to check whether Anchises Analysis public access is available, whether sign-in is required, and the published service limits. It does not query stock data.

inputSchema.description: No arguments. Call directly to inspect the current connection.

tools.name: get_available_exchanges
tools.title: Get available exchanges
tools.description: Use this when you need valid exchange codes or the latest table and date available for each market; call it before passing exchange arguments to other tools.

inputSchema.description: No arguments. Returns every exchange in the current data scope.

tools.name: get_latest_dates
tools.title: Get latest stock dates
tools.description: Use this when you need the latest available stock-data date for one or more known exchanges.

items.description: Uppercase exchange code returned by get_available_exchanges.

exchanges.description: One or more uppercase exchange codes from get_available_exchanges.

inputSchema.description: Provide at least one exchange code whose latest date is required.

tools.name: get_stock_schema
tools.title: Get stock data schema
tools.description: Use this when you need exact stock field names, types, descriptions, or sample tables before screening or writing SQL.

exchange.description: Optional uppercase exchange code from get_available_exchanges. Omit or pass null to combine fields from all sampled exchanges.

inputSchema.description: Optionally narrow schema discovery to one exchange.

tools.name: list_stock_tables
tools.title: List stock tables
tools.description: Use this when you need allowlisted historical table names for SQL or schema inspection; it does not return stock rows.

items.description: Uppercase exchange code returned by get_available_exchanges.

exchanges.description: Optional exchange filter. Omit or pass an empty array to include all available exchanges.

start_date.description: Optional inclusive lower date bound in YYYY-MM-DD format. Omit or pass null for no lower bound.

end_date.description: Optional inclusive upper date bound in YYYY-MM-DD format. Omit or pass null for no upper bound.

cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor returned by the immediately preceding page of the same tool. Omit or pass null for the first page; never construct or edit this value.

page_size.description: Maximum rows to return on this page. Defaults to 200.

inputSchema.description: Filter allowlisted stock table names by exchange/date and paginate the result.

next_cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor returned by the immediately preceding page of the same tool. Omit or pass null for the first page; never construct or edit this value.

tools.name: get_table_schema
tools.title: Get table schema
tools.description: Use this when you need exact column names and types before querying allowlisted tables returned by list_stock_tables.

items.description: Exact allowlisted table name from list_stock_tables.

tables.description: One to 100 exact table names returned by list_stock_tables.

inputSchema.description: Provide exact allowlisted table names whose columns are required.

tools.name: screen_stocks
tools.title: Screen stocks
tools.description: Use this when you need structured stock filters and sorting; prefer it over raw SQL when the requested fields and operators fit this schema.

items.description: Uppercase exchange code returned by get_available_exchanges.

exchanges.description: Optional markets to screen. Omit or pass an empty array to use every available exchange.

as_of_date.description: Optional exact market-data date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Omit or pass null to use each exchange's latest available table.

start_date.description: Optional inclusive start date. Cannot be combined with as_of_date.

end_date.description: Optional inclusive end date. Cannot be combined with as_of_date.

fields.description: Optional output fields. CSV export requires an explicit list; EXCHANGE, Date, and TICKER are always included and count toward export limits.

filters.description: Zero to 30 AND-combined filters. Field names must exactly match get_stock_schema for every selected exchange.

field.description: Exact stock column name returned by get_stock_schema, for example Price_Close or TICKER.

operator.description: Comparison operator. Use in with 1..100 values and between with exactly two ordered values.

value.description: Comparison value for this filter. Use one scalar for eq/ne/gt/gte/lt/lte; null is allowed only with eq or ne. Use an array of 1..100 scalars for in, and exactly two ordered scalars for between.

items.description: One allowlisted field comparison used in the stock screen.

sort.description: Optional ordered sort keys. Fields must match get_stock_schema for every selected exchange.

field.description: Exact stock column name returned by get_stock_schema.

direction.description: Sort direction; defaults to asc when omitted.

items.description: One sort key, evaluated in array order.

top_n.description: Optional global Top-N bound after sorting. At most 200; useful for ranked screens and eligible small exports.

base_query_id.description: Optional prior screen_stocks query_id to refine. New filters are ANDed with the encrypted original query and reuse its exact physical partitions.

page_size.description: Maximum rows to return on this page. Defaults to 200.

inputSchema.description: Build a safe stock screen using documented fields, structured comparisons, and a non-pageable preview of at most 200 rows.

contains_complete_partition.description: Whether the selected result exactly contains an exchange-day ticker universe. Null is reserved for analysis surfaces where this concept does not apply.

next_cursor.description: Always null. Stock row previews are intentionally non-pageable.

tools.name: validate_readonly_sql
tools.title: Validate read-only SQL
tools.description: Use this when you need to check one proposed SELECT or WITH...SELECT before execution; it never runs the statement.

sql.description: Exactly one SELECT or WITH...SELECT statement using allowlisted stock tables. Double-quoted allowlisted table names are normalized to MySQL backticks; string values are unchanged. DDL, DML, comments, and multiple statements are rejected.
examples: SELECT TICKER, Price_Close FROM daily_20260715_asx LIMIT 20

inputSchema.description: Validate one read-only SQL statement without executing it.

tools.name: run_readonly_sql
tools.title: Run bounded read-only SQL
tools.description: Use this when structured screen_stocks cannot express the analysis; it executes one allowlisted read-only SELECT for aggregate or bounded-ticker analysis.

sql.description: Exactly one SELECT or WITH...SELECT statement using table names from list_stock_tables and columns from get_table_schema. Double-quoted allowlisted table names are normalized to MySQL backticks before execution; string values are unchanged.
examples: SELECT TICKER, Price_Close FROM daily_20260715_asx ORDER BY Price_Close DESC LIMIT 20

max_rows.description: Maximum rows returned to the host. Defaults to and cannot exceed 200.

inputSchema.description: Execute one allowlisted read-only SQL query and return a query_id plus a non-pageable result of at most 200 rows. SQL query_ids are analysis-only and cannot be exported.

contains_complete_partition.description: Whether the selected result exactly contains an exchange-day ticker universe. Null is reserved for analysis surfaces where this concept does not apply.

next_cursor.description: Always null. Stock row previews are intentionally non-pageable.

tools.name: resolve_company_identity
tools.title: Resolve company identity
tools.description: Use this when the user supplies a company name or ticker and you need a canonical exchange, ticker, and company name before calling stock-data or company-report tools. It searches only the six supported exchange master tables. Exact unique matches are resolved; cross-market, share-class, prefix, and contains matches remain ambiguous.

query.description: Company name or ticker extracted from the user's request or prior chat context. Do not send the full conversation.

exchange_hint.description: Optional exchange code established from chat context or public-source verification. Codes outside the six supported markets are accepted but produce not_found_in_supported_markets.

purpose.description: Downstream use for the identity. Defaults to stock_data and does not change matching rules.

inputSchema.description: Resolve a company name or ticker against fixed supported-market masters before using the canonical identity downstream.

tools.name: prepare_company_report_generation
tools.title: Prepare host-side company report research
tools.description: Use this when the user asks for company research or a company report and the host has established exchange, ticker, and company name. It always prepares a prompt for live host-side web research; it never reads a cached report, report PDF, or expiry state. Supported active masters select their classified sector, while inactive, delisted, unmatched, and external-market companies use Others. ETF and fund records are not eligible. Anchises Analysis does not search, write, cache, upload, or save the report.

exchange.description: Verified current or historical exchange code. It may be outside the six structured-data markets.

ticker.description: Verified current or historical ticker using letters, numbers, dots, hyphens, underscores, or slashes.

company_name.description: Verified legal or commonly published company name corresponding to the exchange and ticker.

output_locale.description: Required BCP-47 language tag for the generated summary and section bodies. Fixed labels and the seven section headings remain English.

inputSchema.description: Prepare one sector-specific prompt for a compatible host to perform live web research and answer in the current conversation. No cached report is read or written.

status.description: Preparation result. ready includes a host-execution prompt; the other states do not.

message.description: Safe user-facing explanation of the preparation result.

company.description: Sanitized master or host-supplied company context.

identity_source.description: Whether the canonical identity came from a supported master or from the host's public-source verification.

listing_status_verification_required.description: True when the host must recheck listing, legal, and security status before writing the report.

selected_sector.description: Selected prompt-pack sector for a ready result; otherwise null.

prompt_id.description: Stable sector-prompt identifier for a ready result; otherwise null.

prompt_version.description: Sector-prompt pack version for a ready result; otherwise null.

prompt_text.description: Complete instructions for the compatible host's live web research and current-conversation response; null unless status is ready.

next_action.description: Signals that the compatible host—not Anchises Analysis—must perform live web research; null unless status is ready.

tools.name: create_csv_export
tools.title: Create temporary CSV export
tools.description: Use this when the user explicitly asks to download a prior selective screen_stocks result as CSV. Complete exchange-day partitions and large results are not downloadable.

query_id.description: Exact query_id returned by a preceding screen_stocks call in the current access mode and policy version.

expires_in_seconds.description: Signed download lifetime in seconds. Omit this field for the 3600-second (60-minute) default, or explicitly request any lifetime from 60 through 3600 seconds.

inputSchema.description: Create a temporary bearer download from an existing query_id; never invent a query_id.
